problem: It says 'For a fillet weld both parts are shear on the throat, so combine them as vectors.' This contradicts the sentence just before it ('Add the direct stress P/A_w algebraically') and it is wrong. For an out-of-plane load, the direct stress and the bending stress are both produced by forces perpendicular to the weld plane, so at any point they act in the same direction on the throat and must be added algebraically. Only the in-plane case (direct shear plus torsional shear) needs a vector sum.
fix: For a fillet weld both stresses are taken on the throat; they act in the same direction, so add them algebraically: τ_total = P/A_w + M·y/I_w. Vector addition is needed only for the in-plane case of Section 2.

problem: It calls the top of 'either' weld critical. Only the two ends of the weld on the same side as the load line give 46.6 MPa. The other weld, at x = −50, has the torsional shear partly opposing the direct shear: its ends give (−26.5, −14.7) and (26.5, −14.7), that is 30.3 MPa, not 46.6 MPa. A student told 'either weld' would check the wrong corner.
fix: Critical points: the two ends of the weld nearer the line of action of P, r = √(50² + 50²) = 70.7 mm, both giving 46.6 MPa. The ends of the far weld give only about 30.3 MPa.

problem: Wrong percentage. Using h instead of 0.707h multiplies the area by 1/0.707 = 1.414, so the calculated stress is 1/1.414 = 0.707 of the true value: it is understated by about 29%, not 41%. (The true stress is about 41% higher than the wrong value, which is where the number seems to come from.)
fix: Using the leg size h as the throat gives τ = P/(hL) = 0.707 × true stress, so the stress is understated by about 29%; the true stress is about 41% higher than the wrong answer.

problem: Wrong unit. A_line = ΣL is a length, so it is in mm, not mm². Only after multiplying by the throat thickness does the area A_w = t·A_line come out in mm².
fix: A_line = ΣL in mm (total weld line length); A_w = t·A_line in mm²; J_line in mm³ and J_w = t·J_line in mm⁴.

problem: 'd is the distance from each line's own centroid to the group centroid' is imprecise: d must be measured perpendicular to the weld line, otherwise the parallel-axis term is wrong for groups of unequal or offset welds.
fix: d is the perpendicular distance from the weld line to the parallel axis through the group centroid.

problem: The reason given is wrong for the case it names. For two well-separated parallel welds the L·d² term dominates and J_line grows only in proportion to L, so torsional shear falls at about the same rate as direct shear. The L³ growth holds for a single long weld (where r also grows with L, giving about 1/L²).
fix: Area grows as L, so direct shear falls as 1/L. For a single long weld J_line ≈ L³/12 grows as L³ and r also grows with L, so torsional shear falls as about 1/L². When the two welds are far apart, J_line grows only linearly with L and the two fall at similar rates.

problem: Both give 'each 100 mm long' (and '80 mm long') and then use the full length as L, although the chapter defines L as the effective length = actual length − 2h. The reader cannot tell whether 2h has already been subtracted.
fix: State that the quoted length is the effective length L, or take L = 100 − 2×6 = 88 mm in the example and L = 80 − 2×5 = 70 mm in Q5 and rework the numbers.
